_readme: Scope for scripts/audit-gate.mjs. An advisory is set aside only if its package is in buildTimeOnly AND every dependency path to it passes through a buildTimeOwners package (re-checked against package-lock.json on every run). Anything not listed fails the gate. Every entry needs a reason. Do not add a package here to make the gate pass: add it only after confirming it cannot reach a release build. acceptedRisk is different: it is for an advisory that DOES ship and that the owner has decided to accept for now. Each entry names the exact advisory ids accepted, and needs a reason, a revisit sentence and revisitWhen (package -> major version). The acceptance lapses, and the gate fails, when any of those majors changes or a new advisory appears on the package. It exempts nothing else.

buildTimeOwners.reason: The Expo command-line tool and dev server. Runs on a developer machine or build host; not bundled into the app.
Expo's wrapper around the Metro bundler. Runs at bundle time only.
Bundler configuration, evaluated at bundle time only.
Edits the native project during prebuild. Not part of the JavaScript bundle.
React Native CLI commands (start, bundle). Build and dev time only.
The React Native debugger backend. Not included in a release build.
The Babel compiler. Transforms source at bundle time; not shipped.
Babel helper that works out compile targets. Reached through the Babel plugins that react-native-worklets lists as dependencies; those plugins run inside the compiler, not in the app.

buildTimeOnly.reason: XML parsing for plist and Xcode project files during prebuild, under @expo/config-plugins.
Browser-support data for browserslist, used when compiling.
Glob matching in Metro's file map, under @expo/cli.
Compile-target resolution for Babel and the bundler config.
HTTP compression in the Expo dev server, under @expo/cli.
Reads asset dimensions while Metro bundles, under @expo/metro.
Development code-signing certificates in the Expo CLI.
Source maps for PostCSS in the bundler config, under @expo/metro-config.

acceptedRisk.reason: Accepted by the owner on 2026-10-06. Ships in the app through expo-router > query-string@7. The advisory is a denial of service: malformed percent-encoded input can make decoding take excessive CPU time. Per the advisory there is no data disclosure, memory corruption or code execution. Here the code runs on the resident's own device when the router handles a URL, so the worst case is that resident's own app becoming unresponsive on a crafted link; nothing server-side. What was traced in expo-router 57.0.8: the vulnerable decode is bundled and reachable, not dead code. build/react-navigation/core/getStateFromPath.js calls queryString.parse on the query part of a path, and that module is re-exported by the react-navigation/core barrel that the router imports. It is the default path parser for linking, but expo-router's own linking config (build/getLinkingConfig.js) supplies its fork of getStateFromPath, in which the same parse call is commented out. What was NOT traced is whether any path in this app still reaches the core copy with input from outside the app. Start there when revisiting. No compatible fix exists: the patched release, 0.5.0, is ESM-only ("type": "module"), while 0.2.2 is CommonJS and query-string@7.1.3 loads it with require(), so an override to 0.5.0 would break loading rather than fix anything. Do not try that override.
acceptedRisk.revisit: On the next Expo SDK upgrade, check whether expo-router has moved to a query-string that uses a patched decode-uri-component (or dropped it), then remove this entry.
